text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorkInLibrary(x) ::: x currently works in the library.
FromComputerScience(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakingDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x is taking the database course.
TakingClassWithProfessorD(x) ::: x is taking a class with Professor David.
WorkInLab(x) ::: x is working in the lab.
James ::: refers to the specific individual James.

Premises:
¬∃x (Student(x) ∧ WorkInLibrary(x) ∧ FromComputerScience(x)) ::: None of the students who currently work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x) ∧ OfferedByUniversity(x)) → WorkInLibrary(x) ::: All students with part-time jobs offered by the university currently work in the library.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ TakingDatabaseCourse(x)) → FromComputerScience(x) ::: All students taking the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ TakingClassWithProfessorD(x)) → TakingDatabaseCourse(x) ::: All students taking a class with Professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorkInLab(x)) → TakingClassWithProfessorD(x) ::: All students working in the lab are taking a class with Professor David.
James ::: is a student working in the lab.
¬(WorkInLab(James) ∨ ∃x (PartTimeJob(x) ∧ OfferedByUniversity(x) ∧ x = James)) ::: James doesn't work in the lab or have a part-time job offered by the university.

Conclusion:
∃x (Student(x) ∧ TakingDatabaseCourse(x) ∧ x = James) ::: James takes the database course.
